corrected_value.title: Phenomenological space-time: toward an experiential relativity.

decisions.location: Discussion, section 'Resting in a VR environment does not replicate', line 2 (see also Results, line 2; References, lines 26-27)
decisions.quote: Second, the size of the VR did not significantly impact the retrospective time estimation as would have been expected through other studies ( DeLong, 1981 ; Riemer et al., 2014 ). Two differences can explain this incongruence: our study tested a different time scale and used a retrospective, not a prospective paradigm. Additionally, temporal distortions previously reported to be affected by the scale of the environment were realized in nonstatic environments.
decisions.reason: In Experiment 3 (N = 57), the authors experimentally manipulated virtual room size (small room, N = 29 vs. large room, N = 28) to empirically test whether environmental scale affects duration estimation (Wilcoxon rank-sum test, W = 419.5, p = 0.835) and explicitly contrasted their null effect with the prior published environmental-size finding of DeLong (1981). The Reference list confirms the exact identity: DeLong AJ (1981), 'Phenomenological space-time: toward an experiential relativity.', Science 213:681–683, DOI 10.1126/science.7256273. The only shipped row (input_row_index 844) is Azizi, Polti, and van Wassenhove (2023; 10.1523/jneurosci.0816-23.2023), the principal MEG study on spontaneous alpha burst time, and sibling target 2 is Riemer, Hölzl, and Kleinböhl (2014; 10.1007/s00221-014-3848-6); all three are completely distinct studies from different decades and author groups, so report equivalence does not apply. Prior adjudication and state files were checked and are legitimately absent.
